summary: Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied at the INALCO and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as President of the Société Asiatique.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Burgundy, INALCO, and under Yves Hervouet, later serving as president of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

Jeannine Auboyer was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the École du Louvre, University of Paris, and EPHE under scholars including Joseph Hackin and Paul Pelliot. She served as chief curator at the Musée Guimet (1965–1980).

Jeff Dolven studied English at the University of Oxford and Yale University. He held positions as a junior fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows (~1998–2001) and professor of English at Princeton University (~2001).

Philosopher Jeff Malpas earned his BA at the University of Auckland and his PhD at the Australian National University. He headed the philosophy programme at Murdoch University (~1989–1999) before serving as professor and emeritus distinguished professor at the University of Tasmania.
Jeff Watt is a specialist in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Jeff Wilson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and studied under mentors Taitetsu Unno and Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Notre Dame and the University of Chicago, and became Associate Professor of Religion and Asian Studies at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff studied Indology and religious studies, earning degrees from Missouri State University and the University of California, Santa Barbara under David Gordon White. He served as Assistant Professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Hopkins was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Lhundub Sopa at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and served as Associate Professor of Northern Buddhism and Director of the Center for South Asian Studies at the University of Virginia.

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, later holding the J. Newton Rayzor Chair in Philosophy and Religious Thought at Rice University (~2002).

Jeffrey K. Riegel is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Chinese at the University of California, Berkeley (1979–2007) and held a post at the University of Sydney (2007–2017).

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University and under James A. Benn at Leiden University, later holding posts at McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is a philosopher and literary scholar who held positions at Cornell University (~1968–1974), Yale University (~1974–1976), Johns Hopkins University (~1976–1983), and Boston University as University Professor and Professor of French Literature (~1983).

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is an Indologist who completed his PhD at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught Sanskrit and Indian Studies at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).
Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar of Japanology and history-archaeology. He studied at Harvard University and the University of British Columbia, and held a post at the University of Winnipeg (~2010).
Jeffrey S. Lidke is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Berry College and was a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), studying under advisor Sanghasen Singh and doctoral supervisor Collett Cox.
